fact: The Taskbook plugin selects the next Work State and builds the context, prompt, model, and tool set before creating or continuing each Subagent.
Agents report structured outcomes to the plugin. The plugin validates the result, records the next transition, and dispatches the next Work Turns.
The plugin creates the implementer session after the approved design taskbook has been committed.
Pi Taskbook owns four named Pi SDK sessions and keeps each seat’s configured model and reasoning level through Design, Implement and Review.
A designer turn accepts a result only for its pending turn ID and settles it once.
The dispatcher waits for all calls in a batch to settle before processing their outcomes and dispatching another batch.
The original Pi session keeps a tool call active while the named team works. Fact intake waits for the team directly, and a resumed team checkpoint runs through taskbook_run_team.
A distinct work prompt has a distinct Work State. An iteration counter can reuse a state when its work prompt remains the same.
For phases served by buildPhaseInput, the plugin includes the method index in the phase prompt. Named-team workers outside Review can consult taskbook_method on demand.
